newsitem.title: CANADA: Westmin to buy Gibraltar in C$307 million copper deal.
newsitem.headline: Westmin to buy Gibraltar in C$307 million copper deal.

text.p: Struggling copper miner Gibraltar Mines Ltd. agreed Tuesday to be acquired by metal producer Westmin Resources Ltd. for cash and stock worth C$307 million ($224 million).

Vancouver-based Westmin said it was offering C$8.85 ($6.46) for every Gibraltar share up to C$86.6 million ($63.2 million) or 1.18 of a Westmin share based on a Westmin price of C$7.50 ($5.48) a share. The deal, expected to close in mid-October, helps ensure backing for Gibraltar's delayed Lomas Bayas copper project in Chile.

After the announcement, Westmin shares dropped C$1.25 (93 cents) in heavy trading to C$6.25 ($4.63) as shareholders anticipated a 40 percent dilution in earnings due to new shares shares that would be issued in the takeover.
Gibraltar stock gained C$1.40 ($1.04) to C$7.70 ($5.70).

Gold giant Placer Dome Inc. sparked the deal by announcing last week it was seeking a buyer for its 30.8 percent stake in Gibraltar because it was not a core asset. That created new uncertainties for Gibraltar, which was already struggling to find financing for Lomas Bayas. Placer said Tuesday it would tender to the Westmin offer and expected to record a US$11 million net gain on the sale.

After the takeover, Westmin, which produces a mix of metals currently, will become heavily weighted to copper. Westmin currently produces about 46 million pounds of copper a year along with zinc, gold and silver.
Its copper output could rise to as much as 300 million pounds a year over five years with the addition of Gibraltar's properties, making it a strong mid-size copper player, analysts said.
Gibraltar's prize asset is the large Lomas Bayas copper deposit in northern Chile and Westmin immediately announced a 50 percent increase in production targets there.

"Gibraltar is an excellent fit with Westmin's long-term growth strategy. The Lomas Bayas project is a truly exceptional low cost copper project with...great expansion potential," said Westmin President Walter Segsworth.

Gibraltar's plans to develop Lomas Bayas were hampered by difficulties in obtaining financing as one debt deal fell through in July as copper prices plummeted. It recently managed to line up underwriters for a US$140 million debt offering but was still seeking US$55 million more.

"Gibraltar strongly supports this transaction...The combination of Gibraltar's operating expertise and Westmin's financial strength ensure the full potential of the Lomas Bayas project will be realised in the earliest possible time frame," said Gibraltar President Bill Myckatyn.
Segsworth said Westmin did not anticipate any problem in providing the rest of the financing needed for Lomas Bayas from its own resources and credit lines.

A mine at Lomas Bayas is expected to come onstream in 1999, initially producing 130 million pounds of copper a year. Segsworth said Westmin would boost that to 195 million pounds by 2001. Constrained by its finances, Gibraltar did not prove up substantial further reserves at the site, he said.
Gibraltar's other main asset is the McLeese Lake mine in British Columbia, which analysts described as a high-cost, marginally profitable operation producing about 65 million pounds of copper a year.
Westmin had previously said it was looking for acquisitions after the exit of its 76 percent shareholder, Brascade Resources Ltd., last year gave it greater freedom.
